The term “mite” refers to microscopic arthropods having jointed legs and external skeletons that are less than 1 mm long (hence the name). Mites are the most successful and diversified group of invertebrates among arthropods; while some are parasitic, the majority are non-parasitic and free-living. On land and in the water, mites can live and reproduce, and the majority of them do not damage animals. Mites can go unnoticed because of their tiny size.
